# 2 Samuel Chapter 4 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 172r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_004_page_001.jpg

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** When the son of Saul heard that Abner had died in Hebron, his courage failed him, and all Israel was dismayed.

**2** The son of Saul had two men who were captains of raiding bands: Baanah and Rechab, sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, of the sons of Benjamin — for Beeroth is also reckoned to Benjamin. **3** The Beerothites had fled to Gittaim, where they have been sojourners to this day.

**4** Jonathan the son of Saul had a son who was crippled in his feet. He was five years old when the news about Saul and Jonathan came from Jezreel. His nurse picked him up and fled, and in her haste to flee he fell and became lame. His name was Mephibosheth.

**5** The sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah, set out and came to the house of Ish-bosheth in the heat of the day, while he was taking his midday rest. **6** They entered the house as though fetching wheat and struck him in the belly. Then Rechab and his brother Baanah escaped.

**7** They had entered the house while he was lying on his bed in his bedchamber. They struck him and killed him and cut off his head. They took his head and traveled by way of the Arabah all night.

**8** They brought the head of Ish-bosheth to David at Hebron and said to the king, "Here is the head of Ish-bosheth the son of Saul, your enemy who sought your life. The LORD has avenged my lord the king this day against Saul and his offspring."

**9** David answered Rechab and Baanah his brother, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite: "As the LORD lives, who has redeemed my soul from every distress —

**10** when the man who told me, 'Saul is dead,' thinking he brought good news — I seized him and put him to death at Ziklag. That was the reward I gave him for his news.

**11** How much more, when wicked men have killed a righteous man in his own house upon his bed — shall I not require his blood from your hand and remove you from the earth?"

**12** David commanded his young men, and they put them to death, cut off their hands and feet, and hung them beside the pool in Hebron. The head of Ish-bosheth they took and buried in the tomb of Abner in Hebron.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

All three translators agree on the chapter's structure and theological thrust: the assassination and David's swift, principled response. The Mephibosheth parenthetical (v.4) is recognized by all three as narratively strategic. The MT vs. LXX divergence in v.6 (wheat pretext vs. sleeping doorkeeper) is noted by all translators, with all following the MT as primary text.

---
## Disagreement Log

### V.1 — "courage failed" vs. "dropped his hands" vs. "lost all nerve"
- **EMET:** "dropped his-hands [raphū yadav]"
- **LOGOS:** "his courage failed him"
- **PNEUMA:** "he lost all nerve"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "his courage failed him" — LOGOS's rendering accurately captures the idiom. PNEUMA's "lost all nerve" is colloquial. EMET's literal is useful for scholarly reference but awkward in running text.

### V.4 — "smitten of feet" vs. "crippled in his feet" vs. "lame in both feet"
- **EMET:** "smitten of-feet [nekheh raglayim]"
- **LOGOS:** "crippled in his feet"
- **PNEUMA:** "lame in both feet"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "crippled in his feet" — LOGOS. The Hebrew *nekheh raglayim* means "struck/smitten in his feet." PNEUMA adds "both" which is not in the text.

### V.4 — nurse scene
- **EMET:** "lifted-him-up his-nurse and-fled...he-fell and-became-lame"
- **LOGOS:** "his nurse picked him up and fled...he fell and became lame"
- **PNEUMA:** "His nurse snatched him up and ran, but in her panic she dropped him"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "his nurse picked him up and fled...he fell and became lame" — LOGOS. PNEUMA adds "in her panic she dropped him" which interprets beyond the text — the Hebrew says simply "he fell."

### V.6 — Entry pretext
- **EMET:** "coming...taking wheat"
- **LOGOS:** "as though fetching wheat"
- **PNEUMA:** "slipped inside as if collecting wheat"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "as though fetching wheat" — LOGOS captures the ruse sense with formal register.

### V.8 — "gave vengeance" vs. "has avenged"
- **EMET:** "gave YHWH to-my-lord the-king vengeance"
- **LOGOS:** "The LORD has avenged my lord the king"
- **PNEUMA:** "the LORD has given my lord the king vengeance"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "The LORD has avenged my lord the king" — LOGOS: more natural English while preserving the theological claim.

### V.10 — "good news" rendering
- **EMET:** "as-a-bearer of-good-news [mevasseir]"
- **LOGOS:** "thought he was bringing good news"
- **PNEUMA:** "thinking he was bringing wonderful news"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "thinking he brought good news" — combines LOGOS/PNEUMA. "Wonderful" (PNEUMA) over-translates *besorah*.

### V.11 — "righteous man" vs. "innocent man"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "a righteous man"
- **PNEUMA:** "an innocent man"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "a righteous man" — the Hebrew *tsaddiq* means righteous, not merely innocent. David is making a stronger claim about Ish-bosheth's status.

---
*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
